cover.title: 5 niche habits of founders who know their funnel by heart

inner.title: close the funnel
inner.body: in a ga4 closed funnel, users must enter at the first step, and anyone who skips a step drops out of the later ones. an open funnel counts people who join midway, so check which one you built before you trust the percentages.

inner.title: turn on elapsed time
inner.body: ga4's show elapsed time option displays the average time between funnel steps. a step that drags far longer than the rest is hesitation, and it never shows up as a drop.

inner.title: watch the dead clicks
inner.body: microsoft clarity marks a dead click when someone clicks and gets no feedback in a reasonable time: no visual change, no navigation. a button that does nothing is invisible in a funnel and loud in a recording.

inner.title: read bounce backwards
inner.body: ga4 calls a session engaged if it lasts over 10 seconds, has a key event or has 2+ page views, and bounce rate is simply the sessions that were not engaged. a visitor who read your whole page in 8 seconds and left counts as a failure.

inner.title: widen the date range
inner.body: ga4 withholds rows when too few users sit behind them, and its own advice is to widen the date range. a one-day view of a small site can hide the exact step you are hunting.

closer.HEADLINE:
you can't fix a step
you can't see.
closer.SUBLINE: so the founders who win are the ones who check the funnel setting first.
